title.en: All, most, both, neither, each, every and whole
title.es: All, most, both, neither, each, every y whole

summary.en: Use **all / most / some of + the (or a pronoun)** for a group you have in mind: _all **of** the staff_, _most **of** them_. Use **both** and **neither** for exactly two things, and **each** and **every** for single members of a group (both take a **singular** noun and verb). **Every** looks at the whole group (three or more); **each** looks at the members one by one. For time, say _all day_ or _the whole day_.
summary.es: _Todos los estudiantes_ es **all the students** (sin _every_ ni _of_ delante del artículo). _Cada día_ es **every day** (singular), y _todo el día_ es **all day** o **the whole day**.

form: **all / most / some / none + (of) + the/my/these + noun**: _all the tickets_, _most of my friends_
**all / most / some + of + pronoun**: _all of us_, _most of them_ (of is needed before a pronoun)
**both / neither / either** with two things: _both (of) the candidates_, _neither candidate_, _either of them_
**every / each + singular noun + singular verb**: _every flight was delayed_, _each employee gets a login_
**each of / every one of + plural noun + singular verb**: _each of the rooms has a sea view_
**the whole + singular noun** = all of it: _the whole morning_, _the whole of the city_
**each other** = one another: _they know each other_

uses.text: **All / most / some of**: _All the tickets have been sold. Most of the people I spoke to were happy. Some of us stayed behind._
**Both, neither, either**: _Both candidates are strong, but neither has worked abroad. You can take either route._
**Every** for a whole group, **each** for individuals: _Every employee must wear a badge_ (all of them). _Each employee has a different password_ (one by one).

note.en: Each can be used for two or more; every for three or more.
note.es: _Each_ vale para dos o más; _every_ para tres o más.

uses.text: **Time and whole things**: _It rained all weekend. We spent the whole afternoon queuing._ Whole needs the or a possessive: _the whole day_, not _whole day_.
**Each other**: _The two sisters write to each other every week._

mistakes.wrong: I see my friends every days.
mistakes.right: I see my friends every day.

why.en: After every, the noun is singular.
why.es: «Todos los días» es _every day_: _every_ siempre va con singular.

why.en: Every takes a singular noun and a singular verb.

mistakes.wrong: All of people were angry about the decision.
mistakes.right: All (of) the people were angry about the decision.

why.en: Use of after all only before the, my, this or a pronoun, not before a noun on its own.
why.es: Sin artículo ni posesivo no se usa _of_: _all people_, pero _all of the people_.

mistakes.wrong: She has two sisters, and both of they live abroad.
mistakes.right: She has two sisters, and both of them live abroad.

why.en: After of we use an object pronoun.
why.es: Después de _of_ va un pronombre complemento: _them_.

mistakes.wrong: I waited whole day for the delivery.
mistakes.right: I waited all day / the whole day for the delivery.

why.en: Whole needs the or a possessive before it.
why.es: _Whole_ necesita _the_ delante (_the whole day_); sin artículo se dice _all day_.

examples.en: All the tickets have been sold.
examples.es: Se han vendido todas las entradas.

examples.en: Most of the people I spoke to were happy with the service.
All of us were tired after the journey.
Both candidates have experience, but neither has worked abroad.
examples.es: Los dos candidatos tienen experiencia, pero ninguno ha trabajado en el extranjero.

examples.en: Each employee gets a separate login.
Every flight was delayed because of the fog.
It rained all weekend, so we stayed in.
We spent the whole afternoon queuing for tickets.
They've known each other since university.
Each of the rooms has its own balcony.

explanation.en: All the + plural noun means every one of them. Every cannot be followed by the.

practice.prompt: It rained the ___ weekend, so we stayed in and watched films.

explanation.en: The whole + singular noun: the whole weekend. After the, all and every do not fit.

practice.prompt: Both of my brothers ___ in London.

explanation.en: Both of + plural noun takes a plural verb.

practice.prompt: ___ of the rooms has a view of the sea.

explanation.en: Each of + plural noun is followed by a singular verb. Every cannot be followed by of the, and all would need have.

practice.prompt: I go running ___ morning before work.

explanation.en: Every morning means each morning, again and again. All morning means for the whole morning.
